analysis: The PR bumps the landing-site dependency `next` from 16.2.6 to 16.4.1 in landing/package.json (line 13) and regenerates landing/package-lock.json. The lockfile changes include sharp 0.34.5 to 0.35.5, libvips 1.2.4 to 1.3.4, a node engines floor of >=20.9.0, and some new entries. The landing marketing site is not part of the provider/native runtime, the coordinator WebSocket, App Attest authorization, key custody or inference traffic. The threat model scope lists consumer console and admin UI as out of scope. I found no connection to A-001..A-018 or to TB-002, TB-009, TB-011 or TB-012. The visible lockfile tail (head lines 3921-4159) shows registry.npmjs.org resolved URLs with sha512 integrity hashes, so no suspicious non-registry sources appear in that excerpt. The patch excerpt and the first part of the lockfile are truncated, so I could not inspect every changed entry. Dependency integrity for those entries rests on the lockfile hashes. Residual uncertainty: I did not verify the integrity values of the new or changed sharp, libvips and other packages against the registry, and I did not check whether the Node engine floor (>=20.9.0) matches the landing deploy runtime. Neither point is a demonstrated security regression. The change is a routine version bump with no new attack surface evidenced in the supplied material.
